description: Single-panel grouped bar chart (no micrographs or spectra) titled by its caption "Microhardness evolution of the Nb-containing steels". The ordinate is labelled "Microhardness (HV)" and runs from 380 to 500 with major ticks every 20 HV; the abscissa is labelled "Samples" and carries four condition categories in reading order: "as-cast", "723 K/3 h", "773 K/3 h" and "823 K/3 h". A legend in the upper-left identifies two series: "0.02Nb steels" (magenta/purple bars with diagonal black hatching) and "0.04Nb steels" (solid cyan bars). For each condition a pair of bars is drawn side by side, 0.02Nb on the left and 0.04Nb on the right, and every bar carries a vertical error bar. Both series rise monotonically from as-cast to 823 K/3 h; the cyan (0.04Nb) bar is taller than the hatched (0.02Nb) bar at every condition. No numeric data labels are printed on the bars, so values must be read against the gridless 20-HV tick spacing; the citing text supplies them as 406, 440, 455, 467 HV (0.02Nb) and 408, 452, 465, 477 HV (0.04Nb). The figure demonstrates that Nb microalloying at 0.04 wt.% and higher aging temperature both raise microhardness.

observations.observation: The ordinate is labelled "Microhardness (HV)" and spans 380 to 500 with major ticks every 20 HV; the abscissa is labelled "Samples".
The legend contains exactly two entries: "0.02Nb steels" (magenta bars with diagonal hatching) and "0.04Nb steels" (solid cyan bars).
Four sample conditions are plotted on the abscissa in the order: as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h.
Each condition is represented by a pair of bars, with the 0.02Nb (hatched) bar on the left and the 0.04Nb (cyan) bar on the right, and every bar has a vertical error bar.
In the pixels, the height of both bars increases monotonically from as-cast through 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h to 823 K/3 h.
In the pixels, the cyan (0.04Nb) bar is taller than the hatched (0.02Nb) bar in all four condition groups.
No numeric data labels are printed above the bars; the only numeric scales are the ordinate ticks (380-500 HV) and the error-bar spans.
The caption states the figure shows the microhardness evolution of the Nb-containing steels.
The citing text states average microhardness values for as-cast and 723, 773 and 823 K/3 h aged 0.02Nb steels of 406, 440, 455 and 467 HV, respectively.
The citing text states average microhardness values for the corresponding 0.04Nb steels of 408, 452, 465 and 477 HV, respectively.
The citing text states that the microhardness of the 0.04Nb steels consistently surpasses that of the 0.02Nb steels in the same state, matching the visual bar ordering.
The citing text describes the trend as a gradual increase of microhardness of both 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels as aging temperature increases.

subfigures.description: Grouped bar chart of microhardness (HV, 380-500 on the ordinate) versus sample condition (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h on the abscissa), with two series per condition: hatched magenta '0.02Nb steels' and solid cyan '0.04Nb steels'; all bars have error bars and both series increase with aging temperature.

Magnitude of the error bars is not numerically labelled.
